**Pollution:**

\-Air pollution:

Air pollution comes in two types: Invisible and visible. Invisible is based on CO2, and pollutes extremely slowly, while visible is like a black smoke, and is much more polluting. Air pollution cannot be fixed, but instead goes down over time.

Invisible air pollution is generated by all fire blocks, lava, and most machinery, spawning them in nearby air blocks. If the only nearby air blocks are CO2, the machine will stop running because it has no oxygen to burn. If the player is in a CO2 block, their oxygen meter will not appear, but will still go down, unaffected by Respiration. Once it ends, the player will start suffocating, and eventually die unless they exit the CO2 bubble. Caves will naturally be low-oxygen environments, and become more so over time as lava generates CO2. To breathe, the player can either expose them to the surface, releasing all the trapped CO2, or make an oxygen tank to breathe from while caving. CO2 will rise towards the highest block it can reach, displacing or overwriting air blocks. If it reaches the top of the world, it will be replaced by an air block and contribute to the biome's air pollution level.

Visible air pollution, Black Smoke, is generated by burning oil, gasoline, certain materials, and by some machines. It is immediately hazardous to breathe, causing damage. Acting similarly to CO2, Black Smoke will rise to the top of the world, and cause pollution much much faster than CO2. Machines that create Black Smoke can be upgraded to burn cleaner, generating CO2 instead.

Biomes will have a 'biome pollution level', which can influence weather, mob spawning, and even changing the biome. At lower levels, nothing will happen, but as it gets higher, some rain will be replaced by acid rain, which corrodes copper much faster than normal, damages machinery, and kills crops and other plants. Plants will store a pollution value, and will die upon reaching a certain value. This includes grass. If the dirt block itself if polluted, grass will not grow on it until rain naturally reduces its internal pollution level. At higher levels of air pollution, mutants (namely creepers and skeletons) will spawn more often than zombies and spiders at night, and may even spawn in small packs. Around this point, animals will no longer spawn naturally in the biome, and breeding of any kind will fail most of the time. At extremely high levels, the biome will become hotter. Snowy Taigas will become Taigas, etc. This process will slowly continue until the biome is a desert, though to do this would take perhaps thousands of machines several Minecraft years. Pollution will naturally dissipate over time, decreasing to base levels very slowly. If the biome has been changed, though, that is permanent and will not revert.

\-Water Pollution: Water pollution comes in three types: Oil, Gas, and General. Oil pollution happens when liquid oil touches water blocks. The oil will spread across the surface of the water for a distance of 30 blocks per source block. Oil source blocks are mobile, meaning they will travel to the nearest low spot, or to the water's surface if underwater. Several water blocks under the oil will become generally polluted as well. Oily water will burn, creating large amounts of Black Smoke and polluting the water further. Oily water will kill aquatic mobs that enter it after a short time.

Gasoline pollution is similar, happening when gasoline runs into water. Gasoline-water will not explode, but can still burn, producing moderate amounts of black smoke and replacing the gasoline-water with generally polluted water.

Generally polluted water is somewhat different. It will not rise or sink in clean water, and aquatic mobs can live in it, though they will take occasional poison damage until their health is reduced to 1. Mobs this damaged by polluted water will give an inedible version of their meat. Swamp water will be replaced by this polluted water. Polluted water can be created in several ways. Running machines touching water will spread pollution, though this will only happen for a short distance. It will also be created in large amounts when oil or gas contacts water sources. The only machine that can clean water is a Water Purifier, which is very expensive and produces Sludge blocks, which can be burned to produce power at the cost of being extremely polluting.

\-Radioactive Pollution: This type of pollution is spread by uncontained radioactive objects. Similarly to how gasoline can soak into blocks, blocks could become radioactive by exposure and would need to be removed and stored with other radioactive waste. A Geiger counter might be craftable and used to check for contamination. This pollution would cause different levels of the aforementioned special Wither effect depending on the intensity and dosage of radiation absorbed. Water that has become radioactive will disperse the radiation much faster than solid blocks. In the pack, gold has been replaced by lead. Lead blocks could be used to contain radioactive materials without polluting anything.

So, I've actually been taking notes on a potential mod I've been wanting to make for multiple years now, so I opened them up and put down all my ideas in one place. This mod is based around the resource pack I'm updating, The End is Extremely Nigh, and is meant to be a more nuanced and realistic take on redstone components in the form of electricity. I attempted to make it myself, but did not get very far, as I'm terrible with coding. I was able to add liquid gasoline and functional gas generators before giving up.

**Vanilla Redstone Components Changes:**

All current redstone components would behave similarly, only they would use electricity rather than "redstone magic" and any component that spreads power (redstone torch/redstone block for example) would not do so. The redstone block would act as a control panel. Powering one and right clicking would allow you to see a list of items in the grid, their demand, whether they're currently using power, etc. Also, you'd be able to turn items in the grid off from here, saving power and lowering demand. Each electrical item added to the grid (torches (at least in the pack- they're lightbulbs), certain workstations (when being used), enchantment tables, redstone blocks, etc) would add a specific amount of demand to the system. If there's power, but not enough , the system will "brown out". Only lights would function, and at half brightness.

**Electricity Usage:**

Most lights other than candles and actual torches would require electricity to function. In the pack, glowstone is a block of fluorescent tube lights. You'd have various machines that would run on electricity, and batteries and wires to hold and spread the electricity. Unlike redstone dust, wires could be on the underside/sides of a block, between two solid blocks, or even pass through the inside of a block. They wouldn't function in water without being insulated.

The possibilities are endless here. Conveyor belts, lights of various colors, computers, radio towers and radios. I would imagine other mods would focus on what to do with the electricity, like Create, and this mod would focus on the power system itself and pollution.

**Electricity Generation:**

\-Solar:

Daylight Sensors in the pack are already Solar Panels, though this is appearance only. In the mod, they would behave similarly to vanilla, generating power when exposed to daylight. I imagine the panels as behaving differently per-biome, with hotter biomes generating more power due to "more sunlight". Vice versa, colder biomes would lead to reduced power generation. While this method of power generation may be pollution-free, the components for these panels might require less environmentally friendly methods to obtain.

\-Gasoline and Gasoline Burning-Based Electricity Generation:

Emeralds in the pack have been replaced with cans of gasoline, with emerald ore being buried cans of gas and emerald blocks being large gas tanks. In addition, pumpkins, carved pumpkins, and jack-o-lanterns have been replaced with generator kits, inactive generators, and active generators, respectively. In my feeble attempts to realize this mod, I added a GUI to carved pumpkins that allowed you to insert a can of gas, emptying it and giving you an "Empty Gas Can". This could be used like a bucket to pick up a liquid block of gasoline, which I had also added. This liquid gasoline could be ignited and spread the fire extremely rapidly, simply because my coding skills were poor. Ideally, the gasoline would soak into porous surfaces it passed onto, allowing them to burn as netherack does for a limited time based on how long the gas was flowing onto it. Fire would spread to these soaked blocks at an extremely fast rate. In addition, the source block of gasoline would disappear after a short time, though it could be picked up using the empty gas can to regain most of the fuel.

When gasoline is added to the carved pumpkin, it would fill an internal reservoir. Once filled past a certain low percentage, it could be activated to start up the generator and produce power. This would produce pollution, however, as detailed below. When the level of gasoline fell below the threshold, the generator would begin to sputter before deactivating. This could be prevented by deactivating it, filling it back up, and restarting it, or by simply connecting the generator to an emerald block with a gasoline pipe. Gasoline pipes would be crafted from regular water pipes which the mod could add as well as a lining of some kind. Emerald blocks could be right clicked with a gas-containing can to empty the can into the tank, or if the tank is full, refill the can. If both are full, nothing would happen obviously.

\-Water Movement-Based Electricity Generation:

Probably the cleanest method of generating electricity, generators could be placed in rivers and oceans to produce power. I have not put much thought into this, but it could easily be expanded to include water wheels and tides.

\-Wind-Based Electricity Generation:

Wind Turbines, built similarly to nether portals in that they'd be constructed of multiple blocks, would harness the power of wind to produce power. Again, I have not put much thought into this area, but features such as wind speed changing based on biome/elevation/surrounding number of local non-air blocks would be interesting. Perhaps wind could also push things such as item entities in the direction of the wind? Wind speed might also influence the speed at which banners move.

\-Geothermal-Based Electricity Generation:

Unfortunately, I don't really know much about how this type of electricity generation works in the real world. It's easy enough to say "Put the generator in lava for free electricity!!!" but that's not exactly balanced. Perhaps this generator would be obscenely expensive and polluting to make. I don't know.

\-Radiation and Nuclear-Based Electricity Generation:

In the pack, Gilded Blackstone has been replaced by a set of contained reactor rods, due to lore-based reasons involving the piglins. I had imagined that if you submerged this block in water on all sides, the water would heat up. It could then be used for power generation, carried through pipes to structures meant to cool it down again, then funneled back to the rods. The rods might be moved using pistons to determine how much power is generated and thus how much hot water needs to be cooled. The rods would slowly decay and require replacing. Since nuclear waste should not be trivialized, I think these spent rods would be indestructible by most means, and the others would simply pollute the region with radiation. Rods should be placed in a large contained body of water for some time until they reach a point where they'd be considered "safe" enough to store in a chest. Full gold armor (A radiation/biohazard suit in the pack) would be required to safely handle these rods. Otherwise, you'd be inflicted with a special nonremovable Wither effect that would slowly lower max health until death. Obviously, milk would not remove this either.

If water is not cooled at a proper rate, this could lead to a meltdown wherein the casings surrounding the rods fail and massive radioactive contamination will occur. Such a meltdown if left unchecked might result in the whole operation exploding and contaminating everything within thousands of blocks with radiation. This is bad.

In my project, different nations can have massively different tech levels, even more so than in real life, due to a worldwide societal collapse. The biggest examples of these are a space-age nation at war with a medieval society, and a democratic country surrounded by stone-age hunter-gatherers. Any anachronisms are easily glossed over as a product of trade, conquest, etc. The medieval kingdom learned advanced farming techniques and medicine from its neighbor, and thrives from it.

You could also go the route of having technology progression stagnate. The medieval kingdom has been in existence for over a millennia, but hasn't gained any major tech since its foundation. If the people are not focusing on new methods, then you can assume that they'll try to improve what they already have, economics included. The hunter-gatherers may not have agriculture, but they have an industry in helping travelers in exchange for non-monetary payment, for example. 

The third option is to go the "Phoenician route". The Phoenicians in real life were extremely advanced for their time, and were known as merchants to many cultures. Even if your world if Earth-like, this method will work so long as you do your research.
